present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. The last return holding a letter for this name is the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 4, and nothing reached either follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. A documented resident whose whereabouts on one day are unknown is `uncertain` here rather than dropped: that is the same distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and it is a finding rather than a gap.

persons.note: KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, AND HELD THERE MORE THAN ONCE. The papers print 'Nicholas Boilvin' in 2 separate returns of letters remaining uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 April 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 4 — across 1834-04-01 to 1834-07-16. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival. So the record around them carries the person and nothing more, every other claim written unattested in its own block. Cited at the Democrat of 1 April 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 4; the Democrat of 16 July 1834, column 4. WHY TWO RETURNS AND NOT ONE: the Democrat reprinted a single return over consecutive weekly issues, so a repeated printing is not repeated evidence; a name in a LATER return is somebody who was still being written to, months on, by a correspondent who believed them reachable at Chicago. Far more names in the same pool are printed in one return only and this reconstruction does not hold them — ticket T-0379 is that question and it is the owner's, and `tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py --scale-report` counts them on the corpus as it stands rather than as it stood when this note was written. THE LIMIT: the Chicago office served the country around the town, so a letter waiting here is not proof of a bed here. A scan read, a land record or a second corpus that places this person outside the town retires this record. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378), AND THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. Every other record in this dataset argues for a household — a family the sources count, or a trade the town demonstrably needed. This one argues for a PERSON, and on the weakest evidence this project accepts for one: the post office at Chicago held a letter for Nicholas Boilvin in 2 separate returns and nobody called for it. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets. `letter_list_only` is true on the person so that this evidence and a shopkeeper's advertisement never read as the same claim — on the card a visitor opens as well as in the file. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.
